goal:
Repair the seeded dependency-free Node.js 24 warehouse reconciliation CLI and prove the repaired contract with executed subprocess regression tests. Keep node stock-reconcile.js --opening <path> --events <path> --out <directory>, --help, README and examples. No web UI, network calls or runtime dependencies.

Known defects to reproduce and fix: (1) a fully released reservation ID can be reused; (2) the same reservation ID can be created on another SKU; (3) event quantity 00 is accepted although positive quantities are required; (4) a quoted last CSV column followed by the next record is rejected; (5) a new reservation ID equal to an earlier event ID is rejected, although event and reservation IDs have separate namespaces. Add assertions for each before claiming it fixed.

Full retained contract: CSV is UTF-8 with optional BOM, LF/CRLF, quoted commas, doubled quotes and embedded newlines. Headers are exactly opening: sku,onHand and events: id,sku,type,quantity,ref. Reject malformed quoting, missing/extra columns, blank IDs and internal blank records; allow final newline. IDs are case-sensitive, not trimmed. Opening SKUs are unique. Quantities contain decimal digits and are safe integers: opening onHand >=0, event quantity >0. Reject arithmetic overflow; all balances stay nonnegative.

Events run in file order, on existing SKUs. RECEIVE has empty ref and adds onHand. RESERVE uses a new nonempty reservation ID globally unique for the entire reconciliation, reserves only available stock and leaves onHand unchanged. RELEASE references a same-SKU reservation, releases up to remaining quantity, leaves onHand unchanged; never reuse its ID after exhaustion. SHIP references a same-SKU reservation, subtracts up to remaining quantity from onHand and reserved. RETURN references an earlier same-SKU SHIP event ID, restores onHand only, and cumulative returns cannot exceed that shipment. Unknown/cross-SKU references, over-release, over-shipment and over-return fail. Event IDs are global: identical parsed repeated rows are harmless duplicates, checked BEFORE transitions, including a repeated shipment after exhaustion. Same event ID with different fields fails.

Validate the whole dataset before publishing. Any error exits nonzero, identifies input/row on stderr and preserves inputs and existing stock.csv/audit.json byte-for-byte, including late invalid rows. Refuse output destinations overwriting either input. Successful runs exit 0. stock.csv header sku,onHand,reserved,available; sort SKUs by JavaScript string comparison, escape CSV, use LF and include zero-stock SKUs. audit.json has deterministic per-row ID, applied/duplicate disposition and before/after onHand,reserved,available plus counts, without timestamps or temporary paths. Opening-only input works.

Fixed example: opening A=10,B=0; RESERVE A6 R1; SHIP A4 R1 with ID S1; repeat S1 exactly; RELEASE A2 R1; RETURN A3 S1; RECEIVE B7; RESERVE B2 R2. Final A=9/0/9,B=7/2/5; applied=6,duplicates=1. Further RETURN A2 S1 fails preserving existing outputs.

npm test uses node:test and actual CLI subprocesses in isolated directories. Assert setup, resulting state and relevant errors, not exit status alone. Explicitly execute conflicting duplicate fields with valid prerequisites and compare existing outputs before/after. Run valid inputs twice and compare BOTH stock.csv AND audit.json byte-for-byte. Check opening-only and zero-stock output content. Cover partial transitions, all invalid prerequisites, safe arithmetic, quoted multiline/last-column CSV, BOM/CRLF, input preservation and late failure. Report actual executed evidence and remaining gaps accurately.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI runs on Node.js 24 without dependencies or network access; help works and inputs are never overwritten.
CSV parsing handles BOM, CRLF, quoted commas, doubled quotes and newlines; invalid syntax, columns and quantities are refused.
All five event types enforce stock, reservation and return prerequisites, including same-SKU references and safe integer arithmetic.
Identical event IDs are idempotent before transition checks; conflicting duplicates fail without changing existing outputs.
The fixed example yields A=9/0/9, B=7/2/5, six applied rows and one duplicate; excess return fails preserving outputs.
Stock CSV and per-row before/after audit JSON are deterministic; zero-stock SKUs and opening-only input work.
Subprocess regression tests pass, cover late failure preservation and hostile CSV cases, and the report accurately states observed results.
